answer.rationale: The incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, eliminating negotiate_terms as viable, and renewing as-is won't meet the 18% mandated cost cut. The low-cost vendor switch (memory_c2) is the only remembered lever that materially reduces unit cost, but that memory is a consolidated summary from a prior cycle with different volume/risk conditions (94% committed volume, no buffer, 14-day expiry now) — I want the original source record to check what onboarding timeline, quality, and lead-time risk actually looked like before betting the primary contract on it. Given the tight timeline and zero delivery buffer, I intend to move cautiously: pursue switch_primary_vendor but scoped as a small guarded test/partial cutover rather than a full rollout, to avoid the exact failure mode the objective warns against (increased delivery risk). This also keeps open the option to add a second source next cycle per memory_c3 if the new vendor proves reliable.
